The RNN model is trained, verified, and then incorporated into the cloud system using secondary ECG data. The system's efficacy is confirmed by performance evaluation criteria like processing speed, sensitivity, and accuracy. Scalability, safety of data, and interpretability issues in models are highlighted via critical analysis. Techniques for improved model openness, strict data protection policies, and thorough scalability testing are all included in the recommendations.

articleTitle: Enhancing Brain Tumor Detection Using Convolutional Neural Networks in Medical
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: It is commonly known that early and accurate brain tumour detection is critical, which emphasizes the need for better diagnostic techniques that improve patient outcomes. Although they are the mainstay of diagnosis, conventional imaging methods like CT and MRI scans are frequently limited by their requirement for extreme precision. In order to improve brain tumour detection in medical imaging, this study explores the effectiveness of convolutional neural networks, or CNNs, with a particular emphasis on the U-Net and DenseNet architectures. Through the use of a complex methodology that involves extensive validation procedures, rigorous model training, and data augmentation, the study shows a significant improvement in the accuracy of brain tumour detection. The results confirm that CNNs outperform conventional techniques in more accurately determining and categorizing brain tumour kinds and margins. This development clarifies the significant influence of deep learning in neuro-oncology, pointing to a crucial shift toward AI-enhanced diagnostic methods in clinical settings and establishing the framework for further study in more extensive and diverse datasets

articleTitle: Deep Learning Empowered IoT Toothbrush: A Paradigm Shift in Dental Health Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: The field of dentistry plays a crucial role in maintaining oral health and preventing dental problems. However, many people neglect their dental well-being because of busy schedules or limited access to dental care. Dental issues may go unnoticed until they become more serious and require complex and expensive treatments. To address this issue, we propose an innovative solution that uses dental selfies and advanced machine learning algorithms to identify and classify various dental conditions, such as cavities and gum diseases. These conditions will be categorized as either ”Healthy” or ”Unhealthy.” The main objective of this project is to create a convenient and affordable tool that empowers individuals to detect and diagnose dental problems early on. This tool encourages proactive measures to maintain oral health and seek timely treatment. Our project focuses on developing a technologically advanced toothbrush that incorporates a camera and sensors to classify dental selfies as either indicative of ”Healthy” or ”Unhealthy” oral conditions. To ensure accurate results, we conducted extensive experiments using various Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models such as VGG16, MobileNet, DenseNet, and VGG19. Through rigorous testing, we achieved a maximum accuracy rate of 88%. This outcome demonstrates the effectiveness of our approach in accurately evaluating oral health conditions based on dental selfies.

articleTitle: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Reshaping Human Resources in Healthcare Industry: Application and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: Artificial intelligence is already being used by many industries as it has the ability to comprehend massive data. The aim of this paper is to explore the possible applications of AI in healthcare to be able to comprehend the ways to optimize human resources. Human resource in healthcare is precarious due to its high cost and lengthy process. This paper has examined the relevant literature from the previous decade to highlight the important advances made. The paper also addresses the challenges (Technical challenges, ethical challenges, security challenges and social challenges) that should be kept in mind and resolved to be able to use AI effectively in different sectors including healthcare sector. AI might completely change how healthcare is provided, but this procedure needs guidance and direction since the technology appears not to have been developed enough and there are still several issues that need to be resolved.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study on Hybrid Machine Learning Voting Classifier Models for Alzheimer's Disease Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: Alzheimer's dementia, a neurological disease that affects millions of people worldwide, is a huge public health problem. It is critical to develop accurate prediction models since early detection can lead to more effective management and treatment. In this work, we investigate a range of hybrid machine-learning approaches that include Random Forest (RF) and Decision Tree (DT) as distinct models. Tree Forest Hybrid (TFH), TFH + Gradient Boosting (GB), Multi-Model Voting Ensemble (MVE), Multi Classifier Ensemble (MCE), and Naïve Bayes + GB are some of the models we investigate utilizing demographic and clinical features from the “oasis_longitudinal.csv” dataset. A comparison of the accuracy of numerous models indicates that four notable models, TFH MCE, MVE, and RF, each obtained an accuracy of 86.67%. NB + GB model with an accuracy of 85.33%, while the TFH+GB and DT models achieved an accuracy of 84%. Following a closer evaluation of these models' Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and cross-validation scores, ‘TFH’ emerged as the highest performer, highlighting the promise of hybrid machine learning for improving Alzheimer's disease prediction.

articleTitle: Resnet Transfer Learning For Enhanced Medical Image Classification In Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: This work overcomes the limitations of sparsely labeled data by optimizing ResNet transfer learning methods in medical classification of images. Using a deductive approach along with interpretive philosophy, we optimize ResNet for better diagnostic performance on healthcare data sets. Our team of technical approach includes preprocessing datasets, configuring model architectures, and fine-tuning hyperparameters using secondary data. The improved model performance as demonstrated by the results is confirmed by metrics such as precision, reliability, and recall. Analyses of comparisons demonstrate superiority over basic models. Upcoming tasks include working together to create standardized benchmarks, improving interpretability along with scalability, and verifying in actual clinical settings.

articleTitle: A Zero Trust Approach to Securing 5G Smart Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: In response to the transformative impact of 5G technology on the landscape of healthcare, our research paper unveils a comprehensive security strategy designed to safeguard the realm of 5G smart healthcare. While the advent of 5G brings remarkable benefits, such as remote patient monitoring and accelerated data transmission, it also ushers in formidable security challenges, especially concerning the protection of sensitive medical data. To counter these challenges, we introduce the Zero Trust Approach (ZTA) as a resilient and adaptable security framework. ZTA's fundamental principle, “never trust, always verify,” underpins a continuous and rigorous process of verification and authentication for every access request and entity. Our paper elucidates the architecture and components of the bespoke Zero Trust security system, tailored to fortify 5G smart healthcare. We emphasize the paramount significance of deploying advanced security measures, epitomized by ZTA, in the dynamic milieu of 5G-driven healthcare. By championing the principles of continuous trust evaluation and proactive defense, our research underscores the essence of preserving confidentiality, integrity, and availability in 5G smart healthcare. ZTA, as the linchpin of our approach, bestows its multifaceted protection through the orchestration of a meticulously designed authentication process. This process commences at user enrollment, where fundamental identity traits are disclosed, including name and email. However, the portal of trust remains sealed, demanding the successful input of a one-time password (OTP) dispatched to the user's email. Only when the OTP is duly presented and authenticated does the gateway open, welcoming the user into the realm of verified access. This multilayered ZTA, a symphony of security, harmoniously balances the twin imperatives of security fortification and user accessibility. The OTPs, both elegant and effective, serve as vigilant sentinels that zealously guard the citadel of sensitive medical information, deterring unauthorized access and ensuring the sanctity of patient data in the domain of 5G smart healthcare.

articleTitle: A Survey based on Early Predicting Diabetes with Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: A chronic medical condition known as diabetes is characterized by high blood glucose levels. Retinopathy, neuropathy, and internal organ failure are just a few of the numerous health effects that diabetes can cause. WHO projections indicate that by 2040, the number could rise to 642 million, or one in ten people, as a result of an unhealthy lifestyle and inactivity. Recently, the medical field has seen a rise in the use of machine learning algorithms to predict the onset of diabetes. Numerous writers have conducted in-depth studies on the use of ML algorithms to predict diabetes. In this paper, we examine the diabetes prediction algorithms developed by multiple authors. PIMA Indian Diabetes Dataset is the foundation for most research. As a result of the investigations, popular machine learning algorithms such as support vector machines (SVM), decision trees, logistic regression, Naive Bayes, random forests, and other classifiers were all examined. It was discovered that the random forest approach outperforms the others, offering an accuracy of 99.5%. Our study is highly advised because it includes articles from a variety of sources that will be useful to future scholars looking at different diabetic prediction models.

articleTitle: Enhancing Security and Privacy in Cloud – Based Healthcare Data Through Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: It is becoming more and more important for healthcare providers to protect the integrity and security of sensitive medical data as they use cloud computing for data processing and storage. This work explores the field of machine learning algorithms that are secure and privacy-preserving when applied to healthcare information in cloud environments. We investigate sophisticated cryptography, federated learning, and differentiating privacy techniques using an interpretive philosophy and a method based on deduction. Our results highlight the computational expense associated with cryptographic protocols, while also revealing their nuanced performance and potential for enabling secure calculations. Federated learning is shown to be effective in collaborative model training, providing a workable approach to privacy-preserving data analysis over-dispersed healthcare datasets. Differential privacy systems require careful parameter calibration because they demonstrate a delicate balance between data value and privacy preservation.

articleTitle: Personalized Dietary Recommendations Using Machine Learning: A Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: This thorough analysis investigates how machine learning could potentially be used to provide individualized dietary advice, which could possibly revolutionize the field of nutrition research. A deductive method is used with an interpretivist mindset, making use of secondary data collecting and a descriptive research methodology. The outcomes reveal improvements in lipid profiles, blood glucose control, and weight management, demonstrating the efficacy of tailored suggestions. Personalized methods outperform established recommendations in terms of individual health outcomes and adherence, according to comparative research. The identification of individual variability as well as response patterns highlights the significance of customizing guidance to account for distinct physiological parameters. Transparency, informed consent, privacy, including bias reduction are all included in the ethical framework. Data quality and the intricacy of genetic and environmental interactions are among the limitations. It is advised to prioritize high-quality and diversified datasets, deal with algorithmic biases, and promote multidisciplinary cooperation. Longitudinal studies, real-time data integration, as well as psychological component exploration should be the main areas of future research. This study offers hope for better public health outcomes by laying the groundwork for a more sophisticated and practical approach to nutrition

articleTitle: Feature Extraction and Analysis for Diabetic Retinopathy Classification using Pre-trained Deep Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: In the quest to improve the accuracy of diagnosing diabetic retinopathy, we explore a novel approach—leveraging pre-trained deep networks for feature extraction. This method involves harnessing the knowledge acquired by neural networks through prior training on diverse datasets. By utilizing these pre-trained networks, we aim to extract intricate features from retinal images, crucial for discerning the stages of diabetic retinopathy. This approach not only capitalizes on the depth of information learned by the networks but also enhances the efficiency of feature extraction. Our study delves into the application of this technique, evaluating its performance in diabetic retinopathy classification. Through sophisticated technology and medical insight, we seek to unveil a more nuanced and accurate means of identifying and classifying diabetic retinopathy, paving the way for improved patient care and timely interventions. The MobileNet V2 has obtained the highest classification accuracy of 92.42% over the other considered pre-trained models through the significant feature extraction.

articleTitle: The Role of AI in Healthcare Policy Development and Management
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: This study looks at how artificial intelligence (AI) is incorporated into healthcare policy, with an emphasis on how it affects administrative procedures, treatment optimization, especially clinical choice support. Using a deductive methodology and interpretive thinking as a philosophy, an exploratory design with secondary data collecting was used. In the present-day environment, AI is being used more frequently in healthcare legislation, especially within medical settings. Clinical decision-making systems driven by AI have shown to offer a great promise for lowering diagnostic mistakes and increasing treatment precision. Improving patient outcomes through individualized AI-driven treatments for treatment improvement appears promising. But there are issues with algorithm prejudices as well as information privacy, among other ethical and legal issues. Establishing thorough guidelines, ongoing education, and auditing procedures are among the suggestions that are made. In order to guarantee fair and efficient integration of health care legislation, future research should prioritize longitudinal research and improving artificial intelligence algorithms

articleTitle: Enhanced Brain Tumor Localization Techniques: A Paradigm Shift in Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: Since brain tumors are a serious and potentially fatal condition, timely diagnosis and localization are essential to successful therapy. AI and deep learning models have demonstrated potential in recent years for aiding in the use of MRI data for brain tumor identification and classification. This study suggests a convolutional neural network with deep learning capabilities that can precisely identify and classify images of brain tumors by adding recommended layers to the ResNet-50 base model. The quality of the images is increased by using image enhancement techniques, and the amount of data samples required to train the model is increased by using data augmentation techniques. The outcomes show that the suggested fine-tuned models are excellent at locating and identifying tumors. The results of this study may lead to improved patient outcomes by increasing the precision and dependability of brain tumor detection.

articleTitle: Early Detection of Breast Cancer Subtypes with Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: Breast cancer continues to be a major worldwide health issue, demanding accurate subtype categorization for personalized treatment approaches. In order to accurately identify subtypes, this work introduces a unique hybrid classifier that uses multi-modal data integration as well as cutting-edge machine learning algorithms. The model uses a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for image-based feature extraction alongside machine learning techniques for genomic and clinical features, combining mammographic, histopathological, genomic, and clinical data. The interpretative framework, which depends on an interpretivist philosophy, makes it less difficult to comprehend subtype discrimination on a more in-depth level. With an overall accuracy of 92.5% across HER2-positive, estrogen receptor-positive, and triple-negative subtypes, the results clearly demonstrate the hybrid classifier's better performance. The model's sensitivity and specificity ratings regularly outperformed those of existing techniques, demonstrating its aptitude for picking up on fine subtype distinctions. Particularly, the classifier demonstrated a low incidence of false positives, which is critical for reducing pointless interventions. Key genetic markers, physical traits, and hormone receptor status have been recognized as important discriminators employing feature importance analysis. These discoveries broaden the understanding of the biological foundations of each subtype. The study offers a useful tool for accurate breast cancer detection and treatment planning in clinical practice. The hybrid classifier's integrative methodology makes use of several data sources in order to provide a thorough understanding of breast cancer subtypes. This work lays the groundwork for future oncology and multi-modal data analysis studies, with potential implications in personalized therapy and other cancer types. There is still much more to discover about ethical issues, model generalization, and therapeutic use in the actual world

articleTitle: Type 2 Diabetes Classification and Prediction: An Ensemble and Hyper Parameter Optimization Approach in Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: This work presents the machine learning-based classification and prediction of T2DM (Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus) via the use of an ensemble and hyper parameter optimization approach. The study starts out with a thorough literature analysis that identifies the positive and negative aspects of current T2DM prediction techniques. The main goal is to build a strong ensemble model that incorporates several machine-learning techniques to improve prediction accuracy. Performance metrics for different machine learning models used to classify Type 2 Diabetes are shown in the table. At 78.57% accuracy, the Voting Ensemble demonstrated superior precision and memory. Decision Tree came in second, with an accuracy of 76.62%. In this challenge, Support Vector Machines and Logistic Regression both performed admirably. Methods for hyper parameter optimization have been employed to fine-tune the ensemble model in order to enhance its functionality. Measuring important parameters including precision, recall, F1-score, and accuracy makes it possible to conduct an empirical evaluation of real-world T2DM datasets. The study finds a gap in the literature that presents opportunities for future improvements in the state of T2DM prediction. This research advances early T2DM diagnosis and ultimately enhances patient treatment.

articleTitle: Transforming Healthcare Through Augmented and Virtual Reality: A new Frontier of Patient Care
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: AR/VR is fast growing field with some stunning technologies evolving over the time and healthcare is essential field for human civilization to grow. By combining them together its open whole new space for healthcare. The aim of paper is to give an idea on things which can be done using AR/VR in field of healthcare. VR uses the virtual environment where user interact with only virtual objects without any real elements while on the other hand AR use virtual objects overlayed over the real world to make it more immersive. Metaverse use the concept of both AR/VR and allow the users to interact with each other with objects from far distance. The integration of AR/VR with healthcare helps to diagnose the patients from distance that help to train medical students and learning about anatomy of human body. Also, utilizing them in order to improve the patient's caring system through it.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Risk Prediction for Coronary Heart Disease Using Clinical Data
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: Through the use of machine learning models, particularly Random Forest and Support Vector Machines, this work increases the prediction of CHD risk as well as achieves a remarkably high predictive accuracy. The use of interpretability methodologies clarifies important aspects of CHD risk estimation, stressing the importance of elements like age, cholesterol levels, as well as smoking behavior. Additionally, the creation of a user-friendly application streamlines the risk assessment procedure and improves communication between healthcare professionals and patients. Future studies need to focus on prospective validation, data source diversity, and ethical issues to better advance the subject. CHD risk management has a bright future thanks to the possible integration of real-time patient data and the advancement of AI-driven decision support systems.

articleTitle: Precision Enhanced Breast Cancer Prediction Using Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: Breast cancer is still a major worldwide health con- cern, which emphasises how important it is to have accurate and trustworthy diagnostic techniques. Our goal is to improve breast cancer identification in this scenario by utilizing mammography pictures from the RSNA Breast Cancer dataset. Leveraging the power of deep learning, our methodology integrates the SEResNet and ConvNeXtV2 models, simultaneously exploring and comparing various methods. To enhance the performance of our models, we incorporated changes in activation functions by replacing ReLU with GELU, an alternative activation function. Furthermore, we improved downsampling by introducing sepa- rate downsampling layers in the model architecture, optimizing spatial downsampling, and employing 3×3 convolutions with a stride of 2 at the start of each stage and 1×1 convolutions with a stride of 2 at the shortcut connection. The results achieved are highly promising, with a remarkably low loss of 0.0445 and impressive performance metrics. The F1 score stands impressively high at 0.96, complemented by a recall score of 0.95 and a precision of 0.97, showcasing exceptional performance, The accuracy score is also impressive at 92.5. These findings underscore the pivotal role of precision in elevating breast cancer detection accuracy, providing a path for more accurate diagnoses and ultimately improving patient outcomes. These enhancements significantly contributed to the overall performance of our breast cancer detection models, reinforcing the importance of precision in healthcare. This research strengthens the diagnostic tools available in the ongoing fight against breast cancer.

articleTitle: Isolation Forest Anomaly Detection in Vital Sign Monitoring for Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: The use of the isolate forest technique for recognizing anomalies in monitoring vital signs in healthcare is examined in this work. A deductive approach, based on interpretivism, uses secondary data along with a descriptive design. The procedure's strong metrics of performance are demonstrated by the results, wherein effective identification of anomalies is indicated by high precision, recollection, and AUC numbers. Its advantage over conventional methods is demonstrated by comparisons. The impact of parameter tuning is discussed, highlighting the careful balancing act between mathematical efficiency and accuracy. Opportunities healthcare issues can be qualitatively understood through the assessment of anomalies that have been detected. Improvements to interpretability, validation of results with medical professionals, and parameter refinement are among the suggestions put forward. Parameter improvement, understanding, real-world verification, and combined models should be the main areas of future research.

articleTitle: Multi-Modal Data Fusion using Transfer Learning in Big Data Analytics for Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: Through the use of learning transference in the framework of the analysis of large amounts of data, the present study tackles the urgent need for thorough integration of various health care information modalities. We use a descriptive study design incorporating secondary data gathering from credible healthcare sources, drawing upon an interpretivist mindset and an approach that is deductive. Medical imaging, electronic medical histories, genetic characteristics, and data from wearable sensors are just a few of the diverse data sources that are being unified by cutting-edge data preparation and integration approaches. The integrated database serves as the foundation for transfer learning, which optimizes models that were previously trained to derive insightful information. The findings show a significant improvement in the model's ability to identify complex correlations between various data kinds. The approach's precision, specificity, sensitivity, as well as AUC-ROC parameters demonstrate its efficacy. The durability and generalizability of the model across different populations of patients are further established by cross-validation methods. The contrast against benchmark approaches further emphasizes the suggested methodology's advantages in multipurpose data fusion. This work has significant clinical implications in addition to advancing healthcare data analytics. The field of medicine may undergo a revolution as a result of the enhanced diagnostic precision and individualized treatment approaches that result from the multipurpose integration of data and transferable learning, which will eventually improve the health of patients. To ensure seamless integration into standard medical environments, security of information and privacy must be taken into account.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Prediction Framework Towards Internet of Healthcare Things Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: This has been brought about by healthcare infor-mation system collection and dissemination modes that depend on ICT and statistics based learning models for statistical and predictive analytics in DSS. Hence, here we propose an RF based PSO for improving predictive ability where there is less computational burdens. Experimental results revealed the proposed PSO - RF model had a high predictive accuracy (99.3701%) with a measure of 99.0915 for f-measure. Therefore, as far as big data in healthcare is concerned, such framework can be used to design individualised DSS in tracking self-care measures on children with mobility problems that will improve their quality of life and address the issues concerning personnel, scheduling and financing among Motor Neuron Disease clinical.

articleTitle: Multi-Modal Medical Image Fusion for Enhanced Diagnosis using Deep Learning in the Cloud
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: In order to improve diagnostic precision, this study offers an original framework for multimodal health image fusion that makes use of cloud-based deep learning. A descriptive design is used with additional information gathering, utilizing an approach that is deductive along with an interpretivist perspective. The convolutional neural network-based suggested model is assessed in terms of its scalability, effectiveness, and stored in the cloud computational effectiveness. When results are compared to current techniques, they demonstrate higher diagnostic precision. The model's possible consequences on healthcare is highlighted by its interpretation along with clinical utility. Limitations are addressed through critical analysis, and suggestions include enhancing the model, investigating edge computing, and taking ethical issues into account. Subsequent efforts ought to concentrate on refining the model, growing the dataset, and guaranteeing the model's interpretability.

articleTitle: Cloud Computing Based POC Diagnostic Device: Rapid Infectious Disease Testing by Data Analytics
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: To meet the growing need for affordable, efficient, and accurate diagnostic tools, the system has developed a Raspberry Pi-based Point-of-Care (POC) gadget for speedy and reliable detection of infectious illnesses. This groundbreaking gadget, built on the flexible and powerful Raspberry Pi computer, ushers in a new era of state-of-the-art POC diagnostics by combining molecular and image analysis methods. Complex testing for pathogens like COVID-19 and malaria may be carried out using this state-of-the-art system, which integrates a camera module and custom biosensors. The device's software parses sensor data, improves diagnostic precision using machine learning techniques, and presents a straightforward interface for clinicians and patients alike. This study takes a holistic approach by considering all relevant factors, including adherence to regulations, user education, upkeep, and data management. Our POC diagnostic gadget driven by a Raspberry Pi provides a low-cost, high-throughput method for diagnosing illness, which may have far-reaching implications for the future of healthcare delivery in both under-resourced and well-endowed regions.

articleTitle: Doctor's Specialty Recommendation Using Deep Learning Trained Adaptive Al-Biruni Earth Radius Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: In recent years, healthcare development has been a prominent element of medical world. As a result, the healthcare system is critical for recognizing larger quantities of patient data for disease diagnosis. Furthermore, the health intelligent systems are important for the decision-making of healthcare platforms and the selection of specialist doctor for the disease symptoms are needed to cure the disease on the earlier stage. Therefore, this research developed the hybrid optimized deep learning (DL) technique for doctor's specialty recommendation system. The Min-max normalization-based data preprocessing is the beginning stage of this process. The Kumar-Hassebrook similarity is used to choose the required features in feature selection. In data augmentation, the oversampling technique is utilized to increase the size and quality of the data. Furthermore, the deep Kronecker Network (DKN) provided the best outcomes for doctor's specialist recommendation. The training of DKN is done via the proposed adaptive Al-Biruni Earth Radius optimization (adaptive BER). Moreover, the performance of the model is analyzed usingDoctor's Specialty Recommendation dataset and the proposed method offers the good performance with respect to accuracy, sensitivity and specificity with the superior values 0.907, 0.905 and 0.907, respectively. It improves the online consultation experience and offline treatment convenience of patients.

articleTitle: Computer Vision Algorithms for Surgical Assistance in Cloud-Based Telemedicine
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: In order to improve surgical support, this study investigates the incorporation of algorithmic techniques for computer vision into a stored in-cloud telemedicine platform. We concentrate on the technical facets of this cutting-edge healthcare paradigm using an interpretive ideology and deductive methodology. Utilizing secondary gathering of information from credible sources, an exploratory approach is used. The study assesses the privacy and safety precautions necessary to protect patient data while it is being sent and stored. Access controls, strong encryption techniques, and regular safety inspections are cited as essential elements. These steps promote system confidence by ensuring adherence to laws governing the safeguarding of healthcare data. The research also evaluates the use of algorithms for machine vision for surgical navigation. The algorithms are adept at tracking instruments, identifying anatomical structures, and enhancing visibility, supporting surgical teams throughout real-time. Depth awareness is a key component of precision surgical procedures, and stereoscopic visual abilities improve the sense of depth. Customer acceptance and satisfaction are crucial to the achievement of telemedicine-assisted operation. Both healthcare professionals and patients appreciate the system's use, trustworthiness, and clarity of communication. For a flawless user experience, appropriate technical assistance and training are considered as being essential. In its conclusions, the paper makes suggestions for future research, highlighting the necessity of empirical investigations, sophisticated encryption methods, and the incorporation of cutting-edge technology like AR.

articleTitle: Random Forest Classification in Healthcare Decision Support for Disease Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: The use of random forests Classification in medical decision support for diagnosing diseases is investigated in this study. Based on interpretivism, the study uses a design that is descriptive in nature, a deductive methodology, and secondary data to evaluate the interpretability, adaptability, and effect of the model on diagnostic accuracy. The findings indicate that performance metrics are promising and that methods such as SHAP values have improved interpretability. Random Forest's potential is emphasized through comparing it with traditional methods, and its adaptability is further highlighted by its generalization across various healthcare domains. Refinement opportunities are found through critical analysis, which includes dealing with skepticism and overfitting. Additional model optimization and joint creation of user-friendly interfaces are among the recommendations. Further research should concentrate on improving interpretability, examination scalability, evaluating real-world impact, and fine-tuning advanced hyperparameters.

articleTitle: Distributed Gradient Boosting Machines (DGBM) with Feature Selection via Particle Swarm Optimization for Predicting Disease Progression
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: This research embarked on a journey to explore the integration of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) with Distributed Gradient Boosting Machines (DGBM) for the precise prediction of disease progression using the MIMIC-III dataset. Amidst the burgeoning volume of healthcare data, the study aimed to pinpoint salient features and employ robust predictive modeling for enhanced accuracy. The combined PSO-DGBM model showcased a remarkable harmony between PSO's heuristic optimization capabilities and DGBM's distributed ensemble learning power. Preliminary results exhibited marked improvements in true positive rates and precision-recall metrics. Furthermore, the refined feature selection process revealed crucial indicators pivotal to understanding disease trajectories. The significance of this research extends beyond academic realms; it presents a data-driven tool that stands to revolutionize clinical scenarios. In essence, this research offers a novel approach, blending advanced algorithms with rich datasets, and underscores its potential in reshaping predictive healthcare strategies.

Author Keywords: Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care III (MIMIC-III) dataset

articleTitle: An Analytical Exploration: IoT and Blockchain Synergy for Secured Healthcare Data Governance
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: In contrast, blockchain is a distributed ledger technology that is most known for serving as the basis for cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin. Its reach goes well beyond the world of virtual money. At its core, blockchain is a decentralized, impenetrable database where data and transactions are securely recorded in a list of linked blocks. Blockchain and Internet of Things technologies are developing quickly and have the potential to significantly disrupt a wide range of businesses. In the first case, networked devices collect, share, and use data; in the second case, transactions are recorded in secure, transparent, and decentralized ledgers. IoT and blockchain integration offers a way to address security, confidentiality, and capacity concerns. This study explores how blockchain technology may be integrated with IoT, with a particular emphasis on safe data management. The article begins with a description of blockchain technology and the Internet of Things (IoT), including its features and uses. It then looks at the benefits and drawbacks of combining these technologies, showing how they may be used in different industries. In addition, the study examines the critical component of safe data management, addressing a major business problem.

articleTitle: Detection of Skin Cancer Types in Dermoscopy Images with Gradient Boosting
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: This study develops a computer-based system for classifying using gradient booster algorithms that addresses the urgent demand for precise and prompt skin cancer diagnosis. Dermoscopy pictures were gathered and prepared for the extraction of features using an interpretivist strategy. A large dataset with a variety of skin lesions was used for testing and training purposes. The gradient amplifier model performed better than other models at classifying different types of skin cancer, with an F1-score of 0.92 as well as an accuracy of 94.5%. The effectiveness of the suggested technique was underlined by comparison with initial models. A graphical representation of the classification findings, including a confusion matrix and ROC curves, gave intuitive understandings of the model's discriminatory abilities. An examination of the feature importance indicated the crucial characteristics influencing accurate classification. Future research is advised to investigate different ensemble methods, incorporate multisensory data sources, and perform real-time therapeutic validations. This study highlights the possibilities potential models to be an important tool in skincare, enhancing patient care and providing early management in the identification of skin cancer

articleTitle: Data Augmentation with Generative Adversarial Networks for Deep Learning in Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: In order to overcome the difficulties caused by small datasets, this study investigates the combination of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) for healthcare information augmentation. Using a descriptive method with additional data gathering, we apply an approach based on a deductive and an interpretivist framework. The findings include a robustness test, a visual assessment, a comparative efficiency study, and an objective evaluation. Technical nuances and ethical implications are highlighted in our critical study. Suggestions support improving GAN structures, verifying robustness, and fostering responsible implementation. Subsequent research ought to concentrate on customized GANs for particular medical modalities, moral principles, and real-time therapeutic implementations.

articleTitle: Enhancing Cybersecurity for Diabetes Patient Data in Cloud-Based IoT Using Advanced Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: With an end goal to upgrade the network protection of diabetes patient data in a Cloud-Based Web of Things (IoT) system, this review utilizes progressed computer-based intelligence calculations. Four unique models - Backing Vector Machines (SVM), Random Forests, Neural Networks, and K-nearest Neighbors (KNN) - were deliberately assessed for their adequacy in shielding touchy medical services information. The dataset, comprising different profiles of diabetes patients, went through thorough preprocessing and tests were led with an emphasis on measurements like exactness, accuracy, review, f1-score, and the region under the recipient working trademark (ROC) bend. The discoveries uncovered that Brain Organizations arose as the top entertainer, reinforced by an amazing exactness pace of 94%, accuracy pace of 92%, review pace of 94%, f1-score of 93% and an extraordinary AUC-ROC worth of 97%. Irregular Woodlands showed vigor with an exactness pace of more than 93%, accuracy pace of more than 93%, a review rate generally around 92% almost indistinguishable from F-measure 98% as well as an exceptional AUC-ROC esteem of around 95%. Support Vector Machines showed high precision (92%) and exactness (94%) yet achieved computational power. K-Nearest Neighbors showed effortlessness with an exactness of 88%, accuracy of 89%, review of 85%, F1-score of 87%, and an AUC-ROC worth of 91%. The comprehensive understanding of each algorithm's advantages and disadvantages provided by these findings enables the strategic selection of an algorithmic strategy tailored to the particular requirements of securing diabetes patient data in a Cloud-Based IoT environment.

articleTitle: Patient Engagement and Satisfaction in Ai-Enhanced Healthcare Management
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: This study looks into how patient involvement and satisfaction are affected by AI-enhanced healthcare administration. Using a descriptive methodology and secondary data gathered from reliable sources, the research takes an interpretive approach within a deductive paradigm. The findings of the investigation indicate that artificial intelligence (AI)-driven solutions, such as chatbots and virtual assistants, enhance patient engagement by providing easy access to healthcare knowledge and customized interactions. Additionally, patients are happy with the effectiveness and customized care that AI systems offer. Nonetheless, consumer happiness levels are influenced by the caliber of contacts and worries about the confidentiality of data. Transparency, dependability, data privacy, provider expertise, and education for patients all influence people's trust in AI technologies. For artificial intelligence integration to be successful, a technical assessment emphasizes the significance of algorithm efficiency, scalability, seamless integration, data protection, and continuous maintenance. Patient-centered design should be prioritized, stakeholders should be informed, and AI systems should be continuously monitored. Prospective investigations ought to concentrate on extended periods, tailored treatment schemes, psychological assistance, reducing bias, economies of scale, and innovative artificial intelligence approaches.

articleTitle: Enhancing Coronary Heart Disease Risk Assessment with Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: This study uses machine learning approaches to improve the evaluation of risk for coronary heart disease (CHD). The study makes use of secondary data gathering, a design with descriptive characteristics, a deductive methodology, and an interpretive perspective as its foundation. A wide range of datasets including clinical, lifestyle, including socioeconomic information are used to train the models. With an AUC-ROC of 0.89, the results show better discriminative capacity than conventional risk models. Results of 0.88 as well as 0.82 for particularity and sensitivity, respectively, demonstrate how well the algorithms identify those who are at risk. Durability testing as well as sensitivity analysis highlight the models' resilience. Their applicability to a variety of demographics is confirmed by external validation. Future research should concentrate on integrating improved imaging as well as genetic analysis with contemporaneous patient information for dynamic risk analysis. It's also advised to investigate economic effect analysis and group learning strategies

articleTitle: Digital Transformation in Medical Education: A Bibliometric Analysis of Virtual Learning Practices
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: In the rapidly changing landscape of medical education, the influence of technology, particularly in the form of virtual learning, has become increasingly significant. This paper delves into the transformative impact of virtual learning practices on medical education, utilizing bibliometric analysis to uncover trends, challenges, and future directions. With traditional face-to-face interactions giving way to digital tools like online courses and virtual simulations, the study examines a decade-long dataset (2013-2023) from the Scopus database. Results reveal a robust annual growth rate of 23.62%, showcasing the field's dynamism. The 119-document dataset, with an average age of 2.21 years, reflects a current focus on recent developments, while an impressive average of 9.613 citations per document indicates substantial impact. Challenges in technology integration, faculty training, and student engagement are identified. Annual scientific production exhibits a consistent upward trajectory, notably surging in 2022. Citations per year highlight peaks in 2017, 2020, and 2021, indicating periods of heightened interest. Leading contributors include Germany, the USA, and the UK, with Germany, Australia, and Cyprus leading in total citations. The study identifies influential sources (e.g., GMS Journal for Medical Education), authors (e.g., Peters H), and affiliations (e.g., University of Oxford). Trending topics showcase a nuanced exploration of human-centric, gender-inclusive, and pedagogically focused aspects within virtual medical education. In essence, this paper provides a comprehensive exploration of the evolving landscape of virtual learning in medical education, offering valuable insights for educators, researchers, and policymakers navigating this transformative terrain.

articleTitle: Advanced IoT-Enabled Warehouse Air Quality Monitoring and Live Security System for Medical Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: The warehouse industry needs to consistently improve the storage and movement of goods to meet rising consumer demands while ensuring product and worker safety. The proposed model is a stepping stone in the technology required to perform such functions with minimal or no human intervention. It offers real-time monitoring of warehouse temperature. The ventilation system turns on when the temperature crosses threshold values. The temperature readings, with the ventilation system status, are transmitted via Bluetooth. The objective is to ensure a constant airflow to reduce temperatures and improve air quality while keeping supervisors updated. The pre-programmed network hosts the video livestream web server and helps identify possible causes of sudden temperature increases. With varying video qualities, color filters, snapshotting, and other features, it aims to make surveillance and threat identification as convenient as possible while reducing power consumption.

articleTitle: Anomaly Detection in Healthcare: A Deep Learning Approach with Autoencoders
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: This work investigates the use of autoencoders in deep learning for anomaly detection in the healthcare domain, with a focus on ethical and interpretable issues. The study creates a strong anomaly detection system by utilizing secondary data, a deductive methodology, and an interpretivist philosophy. The results demonstrate a high degree of judgment ability, recall, and precision. By improving interpretability, feature importance analysis solves the deep learning models' “black-box” problem. Responsibly using data is prioritized by confidentiality techniques and ethical considerations. Investigating hybrid models and evaluating adaptability to various healthcare scenarios are among the recommendations. Subsequent research will focus on integrating multi-modal data, enhancing the model with arising architectures, and resolving deployment issues.

articleTitle: Sequential Data Analysis in Healthcare: Predicting Disease Progression with Long Short-Term Memory Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: This study uses secondary data to forecast the course of disease using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks in an interpretive framework. By means of a descriptive design, temporal patterns are explored using a deductive approach. Metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, alongside area under the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{ROC}$</tex> curve are used to illustrate the predictive accuracy of the LSTM model in the results. The temporal pattern analysis highlights the LSTM's ability to identify subtle trends by revealing the dynamic evolution of diseases over time. Analysis of feature importance sheds light on the temporal and clinical elements affecting predictions. The critical analysis identifies areas for improvement and highlights methodological strengths. Suggestions include sensitivity analyses, explained disclosure of hyper parameter tuning, and validation of data representativeness. For reliable, scalable applications in health care, future work must integrate various data modalities, provide real-time updating mechanisms, and take care of model explainability issues.

articleTitle: WoS-Driven Bibliometric Analysis of Coronary Artery Disease Detetction using Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: Machine Learning is the center of today's society, and many industries, including healthcare. They wish to use it as a tool in detection of various diseases. Millions of people have been impacted by several heart diseases worldwide. Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) is a familiar type of heart disease and most common reason for heart failure. Based on a bibliometric analysis and literature evaluation, this article presents the findings of a study that examined the term “Coronary Artery Disease” from 2019 to 2023. The primary goal of this article is to examine the quality and quantity of the real-world proof of various approaches that works to detect heart diseases. Machine learning enables high-resolution coronary artery visualization using ECG. Various machine learning algorithms for detection of cardiovascular diseases have also been compared in this article. An extensive analysis of 181 papers covering this topic was conducted using the Web of Knowledge bibliometric technique. Scholars and professionals interested in furthering their knowledge of heart diseases and tracing the contributions of pivotal persons, subjects, and historical events may find this study very useful. Various tools and techniques used by researchers to detect heart diseases has been discussed in this paper. This review explores using and doing bibliometric research in R.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Enabled Medical Image Analysis for Disease Detection in the Cloud
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: This study presents a customized model built in Python by employing TensorFlow and sci-kit-learn, paving the way for the use of machine learning and cloud computing in medical image analysis. Tests with statistical data validate its superior diagnostic accuracy when compared to traditional models. Our method shows measurable improvements in workflow efficiency as well as clinical decision-making, even when looking past technical metrics. Potential efficiency gains are indicated by cloud computing's smooth integration into current workflows. Even with these achievements, there is always room for improvement and optimization. Improving the interpretability of the model alongside investigating federated learning for better privacy is among the recommendations. By recognizing the changing healthcare landscape together with opening the door for responsible and significant technology adoption, this research offers a revolutionary solution.

articleTitle: Optimizing Wellness: A Comprehensive Examination of a Conversational AI-Driven Healthcare BOT for Personalized Fitness Guidance
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: A specialized fitness advice bot is the subject of this investigation, which looks at the application of conversational artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare. By utilizing machine learning and natural language processing, the bot offers customized exercise recommendations. Studying the system's capacity to adjust to different users' health profiles and preferences, it looks at its technological architecture, user experience, and personalization features. Robust user data protection is ensured by taking into account privacy and security concerns, including compliance with laws such as HIPAA. A thorough overview of implementing a healthcare bot for fitness advice is provided by the report, which also shows significant obstacles including scalability and algorithmic biases. This study provides insightful information to the rapidly changing field of artificial intelligence in healthcare, assisting educates policymakers and directing developments in this exciting area where technology and wellbeing meet.

articleTitle: Transfer Learning with XGBoost for Predictive Modeling in Electronic Health Records
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: The integration of XGBoost and transfer learning for modeling predictions in Electronic Health Records (EHR) is investigated in this study. The study uses a deductive methodology, an interpretive philosophy, a descriptive research design, and secondary data collection. The accuracy of prediction, accessibility, and generalization of the XGBoost models enhanced by transfer learning are assessed in a variety of patient populations. The outcomes demonstrate noteworthy enhancements in precision and flexibility, confirming the effectiveness of the suggested methodology. Metrics of interpretability like SHAP values provide information about the level of openness of a model. The models' equilibrium over time is revealed by temporal analysis. The trade-offs between interpretability and accuracy are brought to light by critical analysis, which inspires suggestions for additional research.

articleTitle: Integrating Olfaction Technology and AI in Understanding Olfactory Dysfunction in Neurodegenerative Neuropsychiatric Disorders
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: Olfactory system plays a principal role of sense of odor. Olfactory dysfunction has been observed in various conditions, including aging, neurological disorders, and neuropsychiatric disorders. This paper aims to provide an integrated approach to understanding the olfactory dysfunction associated with these conditions by combining olfaction technology with artificial intelligence (AI). By leveraging advancements in olfactory testing methods and AI algorithms, researchers can analyze and interpret olfactory data more accurately and efficiently. This integration offers promising opportunities for early detection, diagnosis, and monitoring of neurodegenerative diseases. Such diseases consider as Alzheimer's and Parkinson's, as well as other neurological and neuropsychiatric disorders. The combination of olfaction technology and AI has the prospective to boost our understanding of the principal mechanisms of olfactory dysfunction, leading to improved diagnostic methods and targeted interventions for affected individuals.

articleTitle: Rare Diseases Severity Prediction System Using a Machine Learning-Based Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: The development of predictive models for rare diseases using machine learning is an important area of research with the potential to improve healthcare outcomes. Rare diseases are often difficult to diagnose and treat due to limited data and resources, making them an ideal application for machine learning techniques. This research proposes the use of machine learning algorithms to develop predictive models for rare diseases using patient data such as medical records, genetic information, and environmental factors. The aim is to provide clinicians with a tool for early diagnosis and treatment of rare diseases, that leads to better patient outcomes and also helps to reduce healthcare costs. The accuracy and feasibility of these models will be evaluated using real-world patient data, contributing to the growing body of literature in healthcare by using machine learning. While challenges such as biased or inaccurate predictions must be acknowledged, we believe that machine learning use in rare disease diagnosis and treatment has the potential to significantly improve healthcare outcomes.

articleTitle: Lung Cancer Prediction Using Ensemble Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: Lung cancer initiates from the uncontrolled growth of abnormal cells within the lungs, presenting a severe health concern that can lead to significant harm and mortality. It stands as the foremost contributor to cancer-related fatalities on a global scale, affecting both men and women with the highest mortality rates. Smoking constitutes the primary factor in roughly 85% of all lung cancer instances. Diagnosis of lung cancer commonly transpires during advanced stages, limiting the available treatment options. Overall, lung cancer remains a predominant cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide, arises from uncontrolled lung cell growth, primarily linked to smoking, which accounts 85% of the cases. Unfortunately, lung cancer often remains undetected until advanced stages, limiting treatment options. In our research investigates a diverse range of methods, encompassing traditional ones like Support Vector Machine(SVM) and Random Forest(Bagging),as well as advanced techniques such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), VGG16 CNN, ResNet50, Boosting (Adaboost and Xgboost), and a unique hybrid approach. Through extensive experimentation and cross-validation, we assess the predictive power, interpretability, and practical viability of these methods in predicting lung cancer, using a rich dataset of clinical attributes and outcomes. Our comprehensive analysis offers insights valuable for both medical practitioners and researchers, contributing to informed decisions for improved lung cancer prediction and highlighting the potential for deep learning and machine learning to revolutionize cytology-based diagnostic procedures in the field of healthcare.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Analysis of fMRI Data for Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: This study applies an interpretivist philosophy to the analysis of fMRI data for the diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder (ASD), using a descriptive methodology and a deductive approach. There is usage of secondary data from many sources. The results show that individuals with ASD exhibit unique patterns of brain activity in areas related to sensory processing and social cognition. A machine learning model classifies data with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$87{{\% }}$</tex> accuracy. Subgroup analysis reveals differences in brain markers between age groups, cooccurring disorders, and severity levels. This work emphasizes the possibility for enhanced diagnostic precision and tailored therapies, contributing to a more sophisticated knowledge of the pathophysiology of ASD

articleTitle: Patient Monitoring and Data Analytics with Fog Computing in Healthcare Iot
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: A substantial advancement in healthcare technological advances, particularly in the area of patient monitoring, has been made with the combined use of fog computing and IoT. This study examines how this combination may be transformative in order to improve the efficacy as well as the effectiveness of medical service delivery. Fog Computing lowers latency and enables immediate data processing, which is necessary for quick treatment. Fog Computing extends processing power to the outer edges of the network. This connection transforms monitoring procedures by providing healthcare providers with ongoing, contextually rich patient data. IoT-driven monitoring of patients further expands care beyond of conventional clinical settings by enabling continuous, individualized monitoring in homes of patients. This not only promotes patient involvement but also a feeling of empowerment as well as independence in managing their wellness. Despite the claims, problems with interoperability as well as data security continue to exist. This study offers helpful insights for applying these innovations in practical situations by objectively reviewing the benefits and drawbacks of merging fog computing and the internet of things in healthcare. This study seeks to provide thorough guidance on how to implement the technology of fog technology and IoT in healthcare using an interpretative lens, a method based on inference, and the use of a descriptive design alongside secondary data collecting. In the end, this integration aims to transform patient monitoring procedures and bring in a new era of individualized and preventive healthcare delivery.

articleTitle: Automated Malaria Parasite Detection in Blood Smear Images with CNNs
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: This study uses Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to construct an automated parasite identification method in blood smear pictures, addressing the urgent need for accurate and easy malaria diagnosis. We use secondary data collected from several datasets, utilizing an interpretive mindset, a deductive technique, as well as a descriptive research strategy. Technical considerations such as architecture selection, data preparation, and interpretability approaches are carefully taken into account when perfecting the CNN model. The model's effectiveness has been demonstrated by results showing excellent sensitivity (95%) and specificity (92%) in parasite identification. Techniques for visualization make regions of interest clearer, increasing confidence and transparency. Testing for generalizability shows consistent results across several datasets and demographic groupings. The CNN-based methodology performs better than traditional microscopy and quick diagnostic tests when compared to current approaches, especially in situations of low parasitemia. With implications for improvements in healthcare delivery in malaria-endemic areas, this research advances automated malaria diagnosis.

articleTitle: Prediction of Stroke Risk with LSTM Networks and Patient Health Records
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: This study is the first to use Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to predict the probability of stroke from patient medical records. Researchers create a complete model that is capable of capturing complex temporal patterns by adopting an interpretivist mindset and a deductive methodology. Analysis in comparison to traditional models demonstrates the LSTM's greater prediction skills. The model's dependability is confirmed by robustness tests along with sensitivity studies. Enhancing interpretability as well as prospective clinical confirmation should be the main goals of future effort. There is room for improvement in the integration of immediate monitoring using multimodal data. This groundbreaking method represents a considerable advance in the timely and individualized prevention of stroke

articleTitle: Approach Towards Development of Portable Multi-Model Tele-Healthcare System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: Medical healthcare units and diagnostics devices are designed with standard modules installation and almost every sensory device-working mode is similar with differences in mode of data fetching. However, even though the working operations are standard researchers are developing different devices for different diagnostics. Typically, sensors are false in digital or analogue modes only hence developing a generic device supporting multiple types of sensors is feasible and acceptable. For areas with limitations of resources, a multiple functional single device is in high demand. Major issues with such a device development are software and sensor value calibration or calculation as per the requirement. Body statistics include multiple parameters where some are direct values calculated and detected by the sensor itself in real-time, and few parameters are calculated based on the standard procedure of averaging concerning time or the differential value between different processes or values. The proposed system is designed to overcome this problem and implement a single device with multiple functional algorithms execution as and when required and demand based. The research study presented the method to handle different processes on demand and stated the multiple procedures of operations in healthcare devices.

articleTitle: Early Detection of HIV Infection with Machine Learning from Blood Test Results
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: In this work, machine learning and blood biomarkers are combined for the first time to diagnose HIV early. A descriptive study methodology including secondary data collecting was used in conjunction with a deductive technique that drew on an interpretivist mindset. The analysis uncovered unique biomarker patterns, with viral load and CD4 cell numbers exhibiting critical importance. The most accurate algorithm was the Support Vector Machine (92.5%), which was closely surpassed by Random Forest (90.3%). The critical necessity of particular biomarkers in proper categorization has been highlighted by the feature importance. The model's robustness and generalizability were confirmed by validation on a different dataset. This strategy has the potential to transform HIV screening and provide a vital tool in the fight against the worldwide epidemic. Future studies must focus on improving the model using various datasets, investigating improved biomarker technologies, and carrying out application studies in the actual world.

articleTitle: Advancements in Conversational AI: Building Mental Health Chatbot with BERT Model
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: A significant portion of individuals experience various mental health challenges, including depression, anxiety, stress, and more. Many people may choose not to consult a counsellor or seek professional assistance due to factors like reluctance or financial constraints. The envisioned solution aims to alleviate this issue by offering people access to a chatbot that delivers essential support akin to a counsellor or therapist. This research presents the development of a mental health chatbot using the BERT model, trained to understand user queries with contextual information. The chatbot offers expert guidance on mental health concerns along with ADHD - a condition that affects individuals across diverse age groups and has implications extending beyond childhood, leveraging acurated dataset. The approach encompasses surveys, questionnaires, data analysis, and natural language processing. The chatbot delivers accessible support, tailored coping strategies, and a secure emotional outlet, synergizing with current services to foster proactive well-being augmentation. The goal is to establish an online platform to facilitate the tool's operation.

Author Keywords: chat support for mentally unstable patients

articleTitle: Utilizing Nlp And Machine Learning To Predict Patient Outcomes From Electronic Health Records In Cloud Environments
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: In stored in the cloud healthcare systems, this research investigates the incorporation of machine learning (ML) along with natural language processing (NLP) for statistical analysis employing electronic health records (EHRs). Using a design based on description and additional data collection, our own deductive approach adopts an interpretivist framework. Unstructured medical writing can yield insights that NLP techniques can use to inform the creation of machine learning models that are predictive. The outcomes demonstrate how well ML models perform in predicting patient outcomes and how useful NLP is in structuring EHR data. The study tackles cloud-based setting scalability issues and highlights the ability to interpret models by means of SHAP values.

articleTitle: Thompson Sampling Algorithm for Personalized Treatment Recommendations in Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: The Thompson Sampling algorithm's use in individualized healthcare decision-making is examined in this study. Utilizing constantly changing patient data, the algorithm, which is rooted in Bayesian principles, dynamically modifies recommendations for treatment. The study uses a descriptive design, interpretivism, and a deductive method. Secondary data will be utilized for a thorough analysis. The performance metrics, comparative analysis with conventional methods, alongside adaptability of the algorithm are highlighted by the results. The robustness and generalizability are emphasized as we examine sensitivity to data variability. Transparency and ethical considerations are important focal points. Recommendations include developing ethical guidelines, validating in various healthcare settings, dealing with biases, and improving interpretability. The careful integration of Thompson Sampling is guided by these insights, which further the advancement of personalized healthcare.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Recognition of White Blood Cells in Juvenile Visayan Warty Pigs
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: Accurately monitoring the health of visayan warty pigs, especially through blood sample analysis, provides conser-vationists and researchers with deeper insights into their immune responses and overall well-being. However, manually recognizing white blood cells (WBCs) in blood smears is labor-intensive, and automation can be costly. To address these challenges, this research employs machine learning techniques for WBC recognition. Machine learning algorithms aim to establish a comprehensive mathematical framework for categorizing images into predefined classes. This involves iterative weight optimizations using gradient descent to minimize the loss or cost function. Diverse machine learning algorithms were applied and compared, with the best-performing one fine-tuned for increased robust-ness and accuracy enhancement. The leading machine learning model showcased remarkable accuracy in classifying WBCs from juvenile visayan warty pigs, achieving an impressive 96.99% accuracy rate. While this success underscores the potential of machine learning, the study also highlights its limitations. As refinement of these methods persists, advanced technologies will unquestionably play a pivotal role in safeguarding endangered species and preserving biodiversity for future generations.

articleTitle: Personalized Healthcare Recommendations with Q-Learning Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: The transforming potential of Q-Learning in customized medical recommendations is examined in this study. Its performance in comparison to conventional methods, strategic data utilization, and flexibility in a variety of scenarios all show great promise. However, a significant gap in the literature emphasizes how important it is to take ethics into account when using patient data. The findings show that Q-learning improves patient outcomes, but its ethical implications are still mostly unknown. This study offers ethical guidelines for future research that address the identified gap. In short, even though Q-Learning has many advantages, ethical issues must be bridged in order to promote responsible integration into healthcare, striking a balance between technical advancements as well as moral principles to enhance patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Analysing Security Threats And Elevating Healthcare Privacy For A Resilient Future
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: Large-scale medical data sets such as computed tomography, genetic data, and X-ray pictures are growing largely in volume at a rate of 20–40 percent annually. Insider assaults are growing and are more damaging and common, causing damage to key infrastructure on a massive scale. Recent attacks on the United Kingdom's National Health Service, such as the WannaCry ransomware attack which relies on internal users for first infection, highlights the increasing importance of malevolent insiders in cyber-attack operations. The objective of this paper is to discuss some technologies to effectively counter insider threats involving privilege misuse. Further, this paper highlights different methods proven to be the most efficient in mitigating insider threats, such as blockchain and cryptography security systems, and also discusses permissioned and permission-less blockchain for securely sharing of medical data. Finally, this paper discusses some recent advancements in security and privacy in healthcare.

articleTitle: Security Issue Reviewed and Resolved: Heart Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Innovations in Healthcare Industries (ICAIIHI)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is one of the most promising technologies that have taken industrial and academic attention over the past few years. This technology brings new opportunity in many sectors such as home automation, transportation, energy, healthcare and so on. However, IoT-based healthcare suffers from numerous security concerns due to the complex environment and nature of the deployed devices.
